source_observations.observation: Festival as the purpose belonging to the referent. Nominative support and genitive target.
Viśākhā with mantha and Āṣāḍhā with the staff. Two named supplements cover cūḍā and śraddhā.

source_observations.locator: Kumārasambhava 5.30 and the Sanskrit commentary on the verse
source_observations.observation: The ascetic bears a skin and staff. The commentator quotes Amara on the palāśa staff and explicitly assigns the inner staff word to the aṇ rule. The poem gives the compound.
Mantha can be the preparation or the churning stick. Both referents belong to the Viśākhā path.
Adds autsavikam and anuprayojanīyam, gives ordinary utthāpanīyam, and quotes the staff, mountainous churn and spring passages.
The churning mountain occurs inside a locative compound. The commentary explicitly identifies the churning stick.
Feminine accusative ākālikīm modifies the onset of spring. The commentator invokes 114 and also reports a rival ṭhak account of occurrence out of season.
Listed ritual bases, specified compound-final verbal action nouns, the svarga list and the luk list have separate histories. Frozen text doubles t in uttthāpana.

source_observations.locator: Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra 1.22.8,10 in displayed Sanskrit; Oldenberg 1.22.9,12
source_observations.observation: Anupravacanīyam in the request for food, then in agreement with the portion of boiled rice to be cooked. The two sets of numbering identify the same lines.
The locative plural anupravacanīyeṣu generalizes the preceding sacrificial procedure.

Mahānāmnikāḥ describes the years of study; mahānāmnikena occurs in the procedure comparison. Later ākālam marks the study-interruption interval. Different words from the grammarian's person and the lightning.
The food or eating act is related to longevity and fame. The commentator uses the benefit paraphrase āyuṣe hitam and then describes desired outcomes.
The completion of a specified curriculum is the purpose. An ordinary preceding word is required. A preceding bahuc alone fails the guard.
Aikāgārika names a thief. A mendicant with one house as goal supplies a negative semantic control. Two reported derivations preserve the feminine.
For the case of simultaneous beginning and end the examples are thunder and lightning. The additional ṭhan and ṭhañ pathways remain distinct.
Ākālikam describes anadhyāyam in the accusative. The suspension lasts to the corresponding time next day.
The commentator explicitly measures the suspension from the triggering time to the same time next day.
